subject: chemistry

moments.title: Hess's law
moments.body: A Swiss-Russian chemist publishes the law of constant heat summation: the enthalpy change of a reaction is independent of pathway. The result is years before the first law of thermodynamics is formulated.
moments.takeaway: A practical consequence of energy conservation, derived empirically before the principle.

moments.title: Gibbs free energy
moments.body: Gibbs publishes the chemical potential and Gibbs free energy G = H - TS. The most powerful concept in physical chemistry. Maxwell sends a plaster cast of Gibbs's thermodynamic surface to Yale.
moments.takeaway: The thermodynamic conditions for spontaneous reaction get a single equation.

moments.title: Nernst equation
moments.body: Nernst derives E = E° - (RT/nF) ln Q for the cell potential. Electrochemistry meets thermodynamics. 1920 Nobel.
moments.takeaway: Battery voltages can now be calculated from thermodynamics.

moments.title: Third law
moments.body: Nernst's heat theorem (3rd law of thermodynamics): entropy approaches a constant (zero for a perfect crystal) as T → 0 K. Absolute entropy is finally computable.
moments.takeaway: Thermodynamics is closed by a third law.

now.title: Where we are today
now.body: Modern thermochemistry tables let chemists predict reaction enthalpies and Gibbs free energies for billions of reactions. Computational thermochemistry achieves chemical accuracy (1 kcal/mol).
now.open_questions: Can thermochemical data be predicted reliably from first principles for arbitrary molecules?

reflection: Hess derived his law before the first law of thermodynamics. How often does practical chemistry pre-empt deeper theory?
